title_zh: 家庭剧：餐桌上的眼泪与和解
title_en: Chinese TV Dramas (4/20): Tears and Reconciliation at the Dinner Table
note_en: 不愿 (bùyuàn) means "unwilling" rather than simply "not want": 谁都不愿先开口 "no one is willing to speak first." Compared with 不想 ("don't feel like"), 不愿 suggests resistance from pride or principle. Note also 谁都 + negative, which means "nobody": English uses a negative pronoun, while Chinese uses "who" plus 都 and a negated verb.

sentences.en: One group of family dramas focuses specifically on education anxiety, such as A Love for Separation and A Little Reunion, which depict the pressure and conflicts several families face as their children prepare to study abroad or take the gaokao (college entrance exam). These stories strike a particular chord because they tap into an anxiety almost all Chinese parents share.

sentences.en: The relationship between a mother-in-law and her daughter-in-law is one of the most classic sources of conflict in family dramas. Shows such as The Beautiful Era of the Daughter-in-Law depict in detail their many clashes over household habits and ideas about raising children, and how the two eventually learn to understand and accept each other.

sentences.en: As China's population ages, more and more family dramas look at how adult children share the responsibility of caring for elderly parents. These shows often feature brothers and sisters fighting over who should pay and who should do the actual caregiving, plotlines that realistically reflect the eldercare dilemmas many ordinary families are facing.

sentences.en: Because they are so close to how ordinary people live, family dramas are often classed as "realist" works. Rather than relying on exaggerated dramatic conflict, they move viewers through the everyday details of "firewood, rice, oil, and salt" (the nuts and bolts of daily life), which is why the authorities often see them as "main melody" (zhuxuanlü, officially endorsed mainstream) content worth encouraging.

sentences.en: Anna thought that perhaps it was no accident that the most moving scenes in family dramas so often take place at the dinner table, while the shows themselves are so often watched over dinner. In that case, when the family on screen sits back down to eat after a fight, the family in front of the screen is doing exactly the same thing.
